site.name: Cherenkov
site.tagline: Interactive olympiad editorials for informatics, physics and astronomy. Every proof comes with a visualization you can manipulate.
site.ogDescription: Olympiad editorials with a visualization you can manipulate.

home.heroBody: Each editorial is written by someone who competes in that subject. Instagram carries the hook, the surprising idea in a few seconds. This site carries the rest: the full proof and an interactive visualization you can manipulate.

about.title: About
about.philosophyPlaceholder: Neutrino observatories never see a neutrino directly, because it passes through ordinary matter almost every time. What gets detected is the flash of light the neutrino leaves behind on the rare occasion it does interact, and that flash is enough to trace it back to where it came from. That's the idea behind this project. The reasoning that cracks a hard problem is usually invisible, and easy to read past without noticing it was ever there. The visualization is the flash: the moment that reasoning becomes something you can see and trace for yourself.
about.repoBody: Cherenkov is built in the open. Every editorial is a git-tracked file, so the commit history is public. Contribute on GitHub.

footer.madeBy: A public-repo project by the Cherenkov team.

benefits.accessWithoutAccount: You can still access editorials, materials, the syllabus, and interactive visualizations without an account.

benefits.progress: Track completed topics and review your progress so you always know what to study next.
benefits.practice: Save your place in editorials and interactive visualizations, then return without losing your context.
